title: Da Hook
canon: Dashiell Hammett's The Maltese Falcon (1930, public domain) transposed to Red Hook, Brooklyn, in the fall of 1970 — the Knicks' first championship banner is fresh, the World Trade Center's bare steel is climbing past the Empire State Building, the piers are dying underneath it, and the heroin epidemic is cresting. An unreadable investigator — per the working skeleton a marine-claims man walking the piers, not a private eye — loses his partner to a murder over a legendary lost prize, follows a lying client through a fixer, a collector, and a false MacGuffin, and turns in the woman he loves because his code allows no other end. New Renaissance Cinema feature.
look: French Connection austerity: documentary grit, handheld grammar, no glamour, no golden hour. Hard-shadow noir geometry — single or dual directional sources, deep blacks, clean whites, no fill that softens the shadow. Moderate telephoto character (50-85mm), 35mm grain present but not heavy, muted desaturated late-autumn palette. Period-precise fall 1970: WTC is bare steel under cranes and NEVER completed towers, no post-1970 vehicles, no 1940s trench-coat/fedora Bogart aesthetic — this detective looks like he works for a living.
note: Period and place come from 00a-synopsis.md (fall 1970 re-ruled 2026-07-10; Red Hook locus; French Connection register) and the Gate-1-signed brief-001-sam-spade-character-in-location.md (wardrobe, office and under-the-El setups, hard-shadow light law, anti-Bogart rule). reference-on-sharedData.md confirms the Falcon is source text, not a property. Six shots: the pier hero, the two brief-approved character setups, and the three moments the synopsis makes iconic (the partner's murder, the false prize, the handover). CAST CONTINUITY WARNINGS: no cast face is locked — do NOT use 05-investigator.png as a ref, its fedora-and-trench wardrobe is explicitly banned by the brief; character names are pending recast under 1939-film names and Spade's age (42) is PROPOSED pending Founder lock; the heroin-shipment MacGuffin is a working proposal pending Marco, so the false-prize frame stays MacGuffin-agnostic (flour where a fortune should be). COLOR RULING OPEN: the Gate-1 brief locks B&W period-precise as interim default, but every generated still to date (and the site hero) is desaturated color — these prompts are written in muted Eastman color to match the existing set; Marco should rule B&W vs color before a full regen. Known failures avoided: da-hook-piers.png letterboxed and rendered completed towers; twins-dump.jpg (completed towers) must never be attached as a period ref. 2026-07-16 STORY-LAW APPEND: six new story-beat shots added under Marco's Story Law ruling (STORY-LAW.md — every frame must show what is happening and what is at stake), mined from 00a-synopsis.md's Hammett beat map and distinct from the three story beats already in the set: the retainer paid in lies, the 4 a.m. two-murders police brace, the fixer disarmed over his own five-thousand-dollar offer, the drugged glass at the Hotel St. George, the dying captain's delivery through the frosted-glass door, and stripping the gunsel under the El. MacGuffin stays agnostic per the open ruling — the prize appears only as a burlap-wrapped bundle, no contraband depicted. NYPD_1978-1981_12.jpg still not attached anywhere (eight years late for 1970); slugs verified collision-free against existing slugs and 02-stills/_regen/ files.

stills.prompt: Red Hook waterfront, Brooklyn, fall 1970 — a dying finger pier of the Erie Basin at first light, rotting stringpieces, iron bollards, a shuttered pier shed with its name flaking off the corrugated wall. Across the Upper Bay the bare steel skeleton of the World Trade Center climbs above Lower Manhattan, half-built, kangaroo cranes on top, floors open to the sky — the towers are NOT finished in this year and nothing in the skyline is taller than their unfinished frames except haze. The light is a low overcast dawn: one cold grey-pink sky source off the water giving soft toneless fill, and a single sodium work lamp still burning under the pier shed eave, throwing the only warm pool in the frame. No people, or one distant longshoreman walking away. Wide anamorphic composition, grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted desaturated palette, documentary austerity, cinematic, full-bleed frame with no letterboxing, no black bars, no borders. stills.prompt: Under the elevated tracks near Smith and Ninth Street, Red Hook, Brooklyn, fall 1970. A marine-claims investigator in his early forties stands three-quarter to camera on the sidewalk — compact strength, dark hair, unremarkable face that holds attention anyway, expression neutral and slightly amused, the calculation behind the eyes the point. He wears a worn single-breasted sport coat with an open collar, functional and slightly rumpled, no hat, no trench coat — a 1971 Brooklyn working professional, not a 1940s detective. Behind him a row of bow-front brick row houses and a parked 1968 Plymouth; the El's riveted iron structure frames the top of the image. The light is flat overcast late morning coming down through the track structure, laying hard broken slat shadows across the asphalt and across his shoulders; no golden hour, no glamour fill, the shadow geometry tells the story. Moderate telephoto framing around 85mm, grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted desaturated palette, documentary grit, cinematic, full-bleed frame, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: A second-floor office above a dry cleaner in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970. A functional workspace, nothing decorative: a steel tanker desk, a grey metal filing cabinet, two wooden chairs, a rotary phone, a full ashtray, and a frosted-glass office door with reversed painted lettering seen from inside. The only lights are hard low afternoon sun through venetian blinds — raking rigid slat shadows across the desk, his shirt, and the plaster wall behind him — and a small tungsten desk lamp burning at frame edge. Deep blacks, clean whites, no fill softening the shadow bands. stills.prompt: Night on a cobblestone pier apron off Van Brunt Street, Red Hook, Brooklyn, fall 1970. A man's body lies at the foot of a brick warehouse wall, overcoat fanned open on the wet stones, hat a few feet away. Two plainclothes detectives in dark 1970 suits stand over him, one crouched, and a uniformed patrolman holds back nothing — the pier is empty. Every light in the frame is a practical: a single incandescent lamp over the warehouse door throwing a hard cone down the brick, the headlights of an unmarked 1969 Plymouth raking long and low across the cobbles, and a red bubble light pulsing off the wet stone; beyond the lamps the harbor is pure black. High contrast, deep shadow, hot practical highlights. Wide composition, grainy 35mm Eastman color negative pushed for the night exposure, muted palette broken only by the red pulse, documentary austerity, cinematic, full-bleed frame, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: The back room of a longshoremen's bar off Columbia Street, Red Hook, Brooklyn, fall 1970, past midnight. On a scarred wooden table a burlap-wrapped package has been cut open and it is worthless — white flour spilling across the wood, weevils in it, a knife dropped beside the wrapping. Around the table: a vast composed older man in a good three-piece suit who has hunted this prize for years, a small scented fixer gone pale, a silent young gunman by the door, the investigator watching everyone, and a beautiful woman watching only him. The single light source is a green-shaded incandescent lamp hung low over the table, burning a hard pool onto the flour and throwing every face into half-shadow from below; cigarette smoke drifts through the beam and the corners of the room fall to black. Deep shadow, high contrast. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted desaturated palette, chamber-piece staging with documentary texture, cinematic, full-bleed frame, no black bars. stills.prompt: Dawn on a Carroll Gardens stoop, Brooklyn, fall 1970. At the curb two plainclothes detectives put a beautiful dark-haired woman in a good cloth coat into the back of an unmarked 1969 Plymouth; she looks back once. The investigator stands at the top of the stoop in shirtsleeves against the cold, not moving, not going down the steps, his face unreadable. Above the avenue behind them the elevated train crosses, first service of the morning. The light is cold blue pre-dawn sky as the only ambient, one bare incandescent hallway globe burning yellow in the vestibule behind him, and the patrol car's dome light glowing inside the cab — three sources, nothing warm reaches the street. Long lens compression, the woman small at the car, the man large and still in the foreground shadow. Grainy 35mm Eastman color negative, muted desaturated palette, hard-shadow discipline, no romantic framing, cinematic, full-bleed frame, no black bars. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: The second-floor office above a dry cleaner in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970, late morning. Across the steel tanker desk a frightened young dark-haired woman in a good autumn coat counts hundred-dollar bills out of her handbag onto the desktop — far too many of them for the simple tail job she is describing, and her hands are not steady. The investigator's heavier, older partner leans in from the side, grinning, one hand already sliding the stack toward himself. The investigator, early forties, worn sport coat, open collar, no hat, ignores the money entirely and studies her face with neutral, slightly amused calculation — he already knows the story is a lie. The only lights are hard late-morning sun through venetian blinds raking rigid slat shadows across the money, her gloved hands, and the plaster wall, plus a small tungsten desk lamp at frame edge; deep blacks, clean whites, no fill softening the shadow bands. stills.prompt: A tenement hallway off Court Street, Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970, four in the morning. The investigator, early forties, stands in his own half-open apartment doorway in an undershirt and hastily pulled-on trousers, jaw set, giving nothing. Two rumpled plainclothes precinct detectives in dark 1970 overcoats crowd the doorway — the nearer one holds a gold detective shield up into the investigator's face, the second has a flat palm pressed against the door to stop it closing, a notebook already out. The only lights are a single bare incandescent globe on the hallway ceiling burning hard directly above the detectives, carving deep eye-socket shadows, and a warmer table-lamp glow leaking through the door gap from the apartment behind the investigator; the far end of the hallway falls to black. High contrast, hot practical highlights, deep shadow. stills.prompt: The second-floor office above a dry cleaner in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn, fall 1970, early evening. Across the steel tanker desk the investigator, early forties, shirtsleeves, tie loose, has a small immaculate man's wrist twisted flat against the desktop — the small man is dapper and scented-looking, brilliantined hair, a dove-grey suit and gloves too fine for the neighborhood, his face gone pale with shock, and the compact automatic pistol he just pulled is sliding out of his opened fingers onto the blotter. A fat envelope of cash he offered a moment earlier has spilled its bills across the desk between them. The investigator's expression is calm, almost amused. The only lights are the small tungsten desk lamp burning a hard hot pool across the pinned wrist, the pistol and the money, and the last cold dusk through the venetian blinds laying faint slat bands on the wall; the room's corners fall to black. Deep shadow, high contrast, no fill. stills.prompt: A high-floor suite in the Hotel St. George, Brooklyn Heights, fall 1970, night — a once-grand room gone slightly threadbare, heavy drapes, a radiator under the window. The investigator, early forties, worn sport coat, is going down onto the carpet, drugged — one knee buckled, one hand splayed on the rug, eyes losing focus, a cut-crystal whiskey glass tipped over beside his hand with the last of the drink soaking into the carpet. In a wing armchair a few feet away a vast, composed older man in an expensive three-piece suit watches with grandfatherly patience, his own untouched glass balanced on the armrest. Behind the falling man a slight, silent young gunman in a cheap tight 1970 suit steps in with his foot drawn back to kick. The only lights are one fringed floor lamp beside the armchair throwing a hard warm cone over the fat man, and the cold blue night city glow through the window sheers edging the falling man and the kid; everything between the two sources drops to black. Deep shadow, high contrast, no fill.
